title: Sam and the Bees Who Drew Directions
synopsis: Sam the mouse notices a honeybee wiggling inside a glass-sided observation hive, then tries giving directions with a dance of his own.

related_resources.reason: Foraging honeybees use a waggle dance that conveys information about the direction and distance of food.
The repeated wiggle-and-loop pattern offers an optional rhythm for shared attention, not a tested learning benefit.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: “She's giving the other bees directions,” the guide said. “A bee can tell her neighbors where food is by the way she dances.”
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Foraging honeybees use a waggle dance that conveys information about the direction and distance of food.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: The science source supports only the natural or physical phenomenon mentioned in the anchor. The characters, plots and observed details of the invented scene are fiction; no impact on sleep, curiosity or learning is established.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: “Perhaps mouse directions need a pointing finger,” Mum said.
